'''Lisa Orloff Clark''' is a New Zealand mathematician, and as of 2023 is a full professor at [[Victoria University of Wellington]] and head of the School of Mathematics and Statistics. She works in the field of algebra and also on inquiry-based learning in mathematics education.

==Academic career==

Clark completed a [[PhD]] titled ''Classifying the Type of Groupoid C*-algebras'' at [[Dartmouth College]] in 2004.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Lisa Clark - The Mathematics Genealogy Project |url=https://mathgenealogy.org/id.php?id=91211 |access-date=2023-12-13 |website=mathgenealogy.org}}</ref> Clark then joined the faculty of the Victoria University of Wellington, rising to full professor in 2023.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |last=Victoria University of Wellington |date=2023-02-07 |title=Promotion to Professor 2022 {{!}} News {{!}} Victoria University of Wellington |url=https://www.wgtn.ac.nz/news/2023/02/promotions-to-professor |access-date=2023-12-13 |website=www.wgtn.ac.nz |language=en}}</ref> She has published on [[C*-algebra|C*-algebras]], [[Groupoid|groupoids]], Steinberg algebras and [[Leavitt path algebra|Leavitt path algebras]].

Clark is the Head of the School of Mathematics and Statistics at Victoria University of Wellington.<ref>{{Cite web |last=[[Victoria University of Wellington]] |title=Academic profile: Professor Lisa Orloff Clark |url=https://people.wgtn.ac.nz/lisa.orloffclark/about |access-date=2023-12-13 |website=people.wgtn.ac.nz}}</ref> She is on the editorial board of the ''Journal of Inquiry-Based Learning in Mathematics''.<ref>{{Cite web |title=JIBLM.org - Journal of Inquiry-Based Learning in Mathematics - Editorial Board> |url=https://jiblm.org/info/editors.php |access-date=2023-12-13 |website=jiblm.org}}</ref>

In 2018 Clark was an associate investigator on a [[Marsden grant]] led by [[Astrid an Huef]] and Iain Raeburn, titled ''Through the looking glass: sharpening the classification program through implications for operator algebras of graphs and groupoids''.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Marsden Fund awards 2018 |url=https://www.royalsociety.org.nz/what-we-do/funds-and-opportunities/marsden/awarded-grants/marsden-fund-awards-2018/ |access-date=2023-12-13 |website=Royal Society Te Apārangi}}</ref> In 2021 Clark and an Huef were joint principal investigators on another successful Marsden grant, called ''Establishing a structure theory for C*-algebras of non-Hausdorff groupoids''.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Marsden Fund awards 2021 |url=https://www.royalsociety.org.nz/what-we-do/funds-and-opportunities/marsden/awarded-grants/marsden-fund-awards-2021/ |access-date=2023-12-13 |website=Royal Society Te Apārangi}}</ref><ref name=":0" />

== Honours and awards ==
In 2017 Clark was awarded the [[New Zealand Mathematical Society]]'s top prize, the Kalman Prize for best paper.<ref name=":0" /><ref>{{Cite web |title=New Zealand Mathematical Society: Awards and Prizes |url=https://nzmathsoc.org.nz/?awards |access-date=2023-12-13 |website=nzmathsoc.org.nz}}</ref> She was a plenary speaker at the NZMS colloquium in 2019.<ref>{{Cite web |title=NZMS 2019 Colloquium: Home |url=https://nzmathsoc.org.nz/colloquium2019/home.php |access-date=2023-12-13 |website=nzmathsoc.org.nz}}</ref>

In 2022 Clark was awarded the [[Aitken Lectureship]], a joint award between the New Zealand and London Mathematical Societies. Clark gave lectures at [[Queen's University Belfast]], [[Durham University]], [[Aberystwyth University]] and at the [[London Mathematical Society]] annual meeting.<ref>{{Cite web |title=LMS-NZMS Forder and Aitken Lectureships {{!}} London Mathematical Society |url=https://www.lms.ac.uk/events/lectures/forder-and-aitken-lectureship |access-date=2023-12-13 |website=www.lms.ac.uk}}</ref>
